gifts.title: One card explaining how to order, tip, and park here
gifts.for_complaint: QR-ordering confusion + 21% gratuity confusion + unmarked parking lot
gifts.deliverable: A printed half-page orientation card (host-stand, table insert, and a standalone URL page) built from Alma's actual three-venue structure: which of the three doors you're at (café counter/QR, restaurant reserved dinner, hotel desk) and how ordering works there; a plain-English line stating the 21% charge is built into menu prices for staff living wages, not an extra tip; and a small labeled map graphic pointing to the unsigned guest lot behind 528 University Ave SE — since neither Google nor OpenStreetMap show it.
gifts.inputs_needed: Alma's own site (almampls.com) for current venue names/hours/policy wording, plus a public satellite/street view of the address for the lot graphic — both reachable without login.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It answers, in the order guests hit them, the exact three things reviewers say confused or annoyed them before the meal even started — not a marketing flyer, a fix for the specific friction they wrote down.

gifts.title: Tonight's tasting menu, course by course, in plain English
gifts.for_complaint: Portions feel paltry / unclear what's included in the price
gifts.deliverable: A one-page insert pulled from Alma's current seasonal tasting menu that spells out everything actually on the table — amuse bouche, bread and spread, the stated courses, and any complimentary send-off (cookies, petit fours) — printed per season change so a $150–450 guest sees the full inclusion list before eating, not after the bill.
gifts.inputs_needed: Alma's current tasting-menu page/pricing tiers from almampls.com — public, reachable, no login.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It directly answers the reviewer who paid $364 and didn't realize dessert wasn't included anymore — the confusion is about disclosure, not portion size, and this fixes disclosure for free.

gifts.title: Café ordering and today's-sold-out sign
gifts.for_complaint: Bakery sell-outs with no warning + counter friction that reads as rudeness
gifts.deliverable: A small counter/table sign stating both ways to order (counter or table QR) plus a blank line staff hand-write each morning for 'sold out today' — so guests aren't told at the register that the pastry in the case (or the DoorDash photo) isn't actually available.
gifts.inputs_needed: None beyond the café's own posted hours/menu on almampls.com to match wording — public, reachable.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It's a one-line fix for the exact moment — being told 'we're out' with no warning — that shows up again and again as both a stock complaint and a rudeness complaint.
